newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Martin optimistic about Canadian dollar.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Martin optimistic about Canadian dollar.

text.p: Canada's dollar is undervalued and should begin to strengthen on the good fundamentals of the Canadian economy, Finance Minister Paul Martin told Reuters Financial Television this weekend.

"As far as we are concerned, our dollar ought to really reflect our fundamentals," Martin said in a television interview during the annual summmit of the Group of Seven (G7) leading industrialized nations in Denver.
The Canadian dollar has shed almost four percent of its value against the U.S. dollar in 1997. It currently sits at C$1.3891 (US$0.7198).
When asked where he would like to see the Canada dollar trading, Martin refused to pinpoint a level.
"We don't have a target value for the Canadian dollar," Martin said. "Essentially, the market will determine the value of the dollar."
Martin highlighted Canada's stable interest rates, low inflation and improved fiscal situation as the foundations of its economic future.
"I feel very good about where the Canadian economy is," Martin said. "There are no inflationary pressures whatsoever in Canada."
